methodology: DeepMT-DR, a hierarchical multi-task framework integrating Image Super-Resolution (ISR), lesion segmentation, and DR grading. The ISR subnet super-resolves low-resolution (LR) images (with an upscale factor of 4). The lesion segmentation subnet uses a U-shaped structure consisting of 5 down-transition (DT) layers and 4 up-transition (UT) layers. The DR grading subnet is built on ResNet-18. The framework utilizes a task-aware loss (combining segmentation-aware and classification-aware losses) and an overall joint loss function combining ISR, lesion segmentation, and DR grading. It also incorporates a Gradient-Weighted Feature Combination algorithm based on Intersection over Union (IoU) to select features with important DR pathologies.
key_findings: DeepMT-DR achieves at least a 6.8% improvement in DR grading accuracy over other state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Removing the ISR subnet ('W/O ISR') significantly degrades DR grading performance on LR images in the Real-LR dataset, demonstrating the importance of integrating the ISR subnet for real-world scenarios. The proposed task-aware loss provides an effective way to supervise super-resolved images, encouraging the ISR subnet to handle clinical LR images with unknown degradation.
